description: The chart illustrates the difference in average word error rate (WER) from “Whisper large” for two fine-tuned models across several text optimisations. The category axis is vertical and labeled “Optimisations applied,” listing (top to bottom) Normalised, Add Spacing, Remove Spacing, Americanisms, and Dates. The value axis is horizontal and labeled “Difference in Average WER from Whisper large,” shown on a linear scale with tick labels at approximately 0.000, 0.001, and 0.002 (units not explicitly stated). Each category contains two horizontally aligned bars: an orange bar for the “NESAC ft model” and a green bar for the “SESHA ft model,” as indicated by the legend titled “Model” below the plot; each bar has a numeric value label at its right end. For Normalised, the NESAC bar is about 0.00334 and the SESHA bar about 0.00323; for Add Spacing, NESAC is about 0.00319 and SESHA about 0.00344; for Remove Spacing, NESAC is about 0.00311 and SESHA about 0.00306; for Americanisms, NESAC is about 0.00299 and SESHA about 0.00302; and for Dates, NESAC is about 0.00257 and SESHA about 0.00228. The bars are grouped by optimisation (paired orange/green per row), the categories appear in the listed order rather than being sorted by bar length, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond the consistent color coding and value annotations.
